subject: divorced dads
one_liner: Custody weekends, restructured as a competitive live-service season.
brand_voice_notes: Deadpan live-service operator that has decided the standard visitation schedule is a game mode and files a child under squadmate. Every piece of copy is written by a product team that genuinely believes a shrinking storm circle solves unstructured Saturdays. The court order is referred to as the ruleset, the driveway is referred to as the extraction point, and nobody ever acknowledges that this is sad. Progression language is used with total sincerity for things that cannot be progressed. Prices are stated with the confidence of a company that has cleared them with counsel. No winking, no self-awareness, no jokes told at the product's expense.

hero.h1: Every other weekend is a match.
hero.sub: Duos restructures standard visitation as a 48-hour ranked co-op season with a published storm timer, a 100-tier progression track, and a fixed extraction point at 6:00 PM Sunday. Queue opens Friday.

features.title: The Storm
features.blurb: Your play area contracts on a published timer from Friday 6:00 PM until it closes on the driveway Sunday at 6:00 PM. Dads operating inside the circle report 40% fewer unstructured silences and 3.2 fewer trips to the same Target.

features.title: Season Pass
features.blurb: The custody agreement rendered as 100 tiers. A recital unlocks Tier 14. A dentist appointment you were told about in advance unlocks Tier 31. Nobody has reached Tier 100. The ruleset does not contain a Tier 100.

features.title: Emote Wheel
features.blurb: Eight approved gestures for the handoff, mapped to a radial selector you can operate from the driver's seat. Free text with your co-parent is disabled at every price point, including the one that costs $1,400.

pricing_tiers.name: Standard Visitation
pricing_tiers.tagline: The mode everyone is placed in by default.
perks: Emote wheel limited to two gestures

pricing_tiers.name: Every Other Weekend Plus
pricing_tiers.tagline: For dads holding a Wednesday dinner.
perks: Wednesday dinner scored as a mid-season event

pricing_tiers.name: Founder's Custody Bundle
pricing_tiers.tagline: Priced by your attorney, collected by us.
perks: All 100 tiers unlocked, still no Tier 100
Priority extraction lane at the driveway
Does not modify the underlying court order

demo_screen_concept: The pre-drop lobby, built as a game launcher. A large avatar plate shows the dad standing in a rendered one-bedroom apartment with a couch, a folded air mattress and one framed photo. A squad rail on the left holds two slots: his (READY) and his son's (EN ROUTE, ETA 6:14 PM). A storm timer at the top counts down live to Sunday 6:00 PM EXTRACTION. A tab bar switches between LOBBY, SEASON PASS and LOADOUT: the season pass tab is a horizontally scrollable 100-tier rail where tiers 1 through 62 are claimed and everything past 62 is locked with a padlock and a reason; the loadout tab is a grid of rarity-graded items that are actually in the apartment (Legendary Air Mattress, Epic Nintendo Switch, Rare Second Toothbrush, Common Streaming Password, Uncommon Booster Seat) with hover tooltips giving acquisition date and durability. An EMOTE button opens a radial wheel of eight approved driveway gestures, each selectable, each with a deadpan description. A READY UP button at the bottom toggles between READY and STANDING BY, and the storm timer keeps ticking either way.

images.rationale: The day's style archetype is extruded clay, so the medium for every slot is a soft 3D clay-render, not photography. Hero: taken, but as a 1:1 clay avatar seated inside the hero storm ring rather than a 16:9 landscape plate, because the composition is a launcher portrait and a wide photographic band would fight the tile stack. Demo subject assets: no separate generation, because the pre-drop lobby's only photo-shaped slot is the player avatar plate and the squad rail, both of which reuse the hero avatar so the same man appears in the pitch and in his own lobby. Testimonials: all three named users given clay headshots, which is where the remaining budget went. Four images, one reused across two surfaces.

items.prompt: Soft 3D clay-render character portrait, matte modeling-clay material with chunky rounded forms and softly sculpted edges. A single middle-aged man with a receding hairline and a neat goatee, wearing a plain cobalt blue polo shirt, standing squarely facing the viewer with a flat neutral expression, a rolled sleeping mat tucked under one arm. One focal subject, centered, three-quarter body crop. Even soft studio lighting, cool soft shadows, no hard edges anywhere. Seamless pale periwinkle backdrop hex E9EDFB. Cobalt blue hex 2F55E8 on the polo. One small magenta hex FF2E74 detail on his wristband. Toy-like, tactile, sincere, not comedic. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.
items.verdict: pass on first attempt: correct subject, cobalt polo and magenta wristband land the palette discipline, rolled mat reads as the air-mattress bit, deadpan expression, clean periwinkle seamless, no text artifacts. Reused as the demo lobby avatar and squad-rail portrait.

items.verdict: pass on first attempt: HVAC-manager read is exact, blue work shirt holds the palette, expression is flat. Slightly more sculpted realism than the hero, kept because the variance reads as different players rather than different renderers.

items.prompt: Soft 3D clay-render character portrait, matte modeling-clay material with chunky rounded simplified forms and softly sculpted edges. Head and shoulders of a single middle-aged man with shaggy shoulder-length brown hair and light stubble, wearing a plain cobalt blue hex 2F55E8 crew-neck sweatshirt with a gaming headset resting around his neck, facing the viewer with a flat neutral expression. One focal subject, centered, tight headshot. Even soft studio lighting, cool soft shadows, no hard edges. Seamless pale periwinkle backdrop hex E9EDFB. Magenta hex FF2E74 accent on the headset earcup. CORRECTIONS: do not render raw unpainted terracotta or monochrome brown clay, the figure must be fully coloured with a cool cobalt blue garment against the pale periwinkle backdrop; keep the face smooth, simplified and toy-like rather than a detailed realistic sculpture; keep the overall image cool and light in value, not warm and earthy; keep the expression calm and deadpan, not pained or scowling. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.
items.verdict: attempt 1 failed the palette-harmony check: it came back as an unpainted warm terracotta bust with a realistic pained sculpt, the only warm image on a cool page and reading as a different medium from the other three. Regenerated once with explicit corrective feedback on colour, value and facial simplification. Attempt 2 passes: cobalt sweatshirt, magenta earcups carrying the rationed accent, smooth toy-like face, calm expression, cool light values.

design_direction.style: Extruded clay game-launcher, season-announcement daylight mode. The page is staged as the live-service season page of a heavily funded games company that has decided the custody schedule is a game mode and files a nine-year-old under squadmate. A pale periwinkle ground (#E9EDFB) runs the whole page with no dark mode, no glass, no blur panels, no aurora washes, no paper stock, no print rules, no drawing-sheet chrome and no bento lattice: every surface is an extruded clay slab in near-white (#F7F9FF) with a generous 26px radius on plates and 999px on pills, lifted by a paired soft shadow (a 20px cool drop below and a 1px inset highlight along the top edge) so nothing has a hard edge anywhere on the page. Corners are never square, borders are never hairlines, and depth never comes from a line. The organizing move is the tile stack: content is laid out as chunky rounded slabs of unequal height butted at a 20px gutter, each one sitting slightly proud of the ground, so every section reads as a panel in a game launcher rather than a section on a website. The core motif is the tier node: a fat rounded capsule carrying a numeral, filled cobalt when claimed and left as unpressed clay when locked, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing tier badge, the testimonial rating and the season-pass rail unit, so every quantity on the page is expressed as progression. The second motif is the storm ring: a thick concentric double ring built in pure CSS border-radius that contracts on reveal, hemming section breaks and framing every avatar, so the reader is always inside a closing circle. One cobalt (#2F55E8) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every primary CTA, one word per headline, and every claimed tier node, always as a solid clay flood with periwinkle knocked out of it. One rationed custody magenta (#FF2E74) is quarantined strictly to schedule telemetry (the storm countdown, locked tiers, the not-your-weekend state, missed-session counts, the disabled free-text row in pricing) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only warm colour on a cool page is always the schedule saying no. Fredoka sets the wordmark and headlines in heavy rounded display at monumental sizes with publisher confidence, tracking tightened to -0.02em at display sizes. Nunito Sans carries plain, faintly patch-notes body copy at 17px with a 1.62 line-height. Every figure that pretends to be season telemetry (tier numbers, storm countdowns, ETAs, durability percentages, match lengths, tier prices) is set in Spline Sans Mono with tabular figures inside recessed clay wells one step darker than the slab, so it reads like the launcher, not marketing. Motion is toy-restrained: slabs squish to scale 0.97 on press and spring back on a cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) curve, tier nodes fill left to right once on scroll, storm rings contract 8px on reveal, CTAs depress 2px into their own shadow, the magenta countdown digit steps once per second, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no gradients on type, no hard offset sticker shadows, no bento lattice, no hairline rules, no hatch fills, no didone engraving, no split-flap numerals, no supergraphic arcs, no roundels, no HUD corner brackets, no drawing-sheet title blocks, no engraved seals, no mirrored type, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your kid under 'squadmate' and considers Sunday 6:00 PM a scheduled extraction.

fonts.body: 'Nunito Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Live-service game season page: clay hero slab with a monumental rounded-display claim beside a CSS-built storm ring and a season telemetry strip in mono, three feature slabs indexed with tier nodes, testimonial slabs with clay-framed player portraits and season credentials, three pricing slabs laid out as season editions with tier-node badges, closing CTA slab, handoff to the pre-drop lobby demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Spring squish on press (scale 0.97, cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)), tier nodes filling left to right on scroll, storm rings contracting 8px on reveal, CTAs depressing 2px into their own shadow, a magenta countdown stepping once per second, 6px fade-up with 40ms stagger, everything gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Asymmetric two-slab hero on periwinkle: left slab carries the monumental Fredoka claim with one word flooded cobalt, the sub in Nunito Sans at a 62-character measure, and a cobalt clay pill CTA; right slab carries a CSS-built storm ring with the player portrait seated at its centre and a live magenta countdown to extraction beneath it. A four-cell season telemetry strip in Spline Sans Mono sits under both, recessed into the ground.
